title: First Contact on 14th Street
hook: Your craft landed at midday. You have four hours, twenty dollars of local currency, and orders to explain this species to high command.
premise: Assume Earth is entirely uncataloged. The tall bipeds moving along 14th Street into the East Village are not your neighbors or fellow students. They are an baffling terrestrial species engaged in ritual consumption, fur worship, and daily skin-swapping. You are here to take physical inventory.
ending: Field report concluded. The species is fragile, carbon-based, and hopelessly devoted to four-legged rulers. Re-entry sequence begins.

stops.title: The Sorting Ground
stops.place: Union Square South Plaza, 14th St & Broadway
stops.body: Subterranean tubes discharge hundreds of bipeds every sixty seconds onto a slab of stone. They scatter without colliding, guided by handheld glowing tablets that dictate their velocity and path.
stops.move: Stand near the south steps. Count forty bipeds with glowing screens before taking a single step forward.
stops.image_query: Union Square pedestrian plaza New York

stops.title: Exoskeleton Replacement Center
stops.place: St. Marks Place, between 3rd Ave & 2nd Ave
stops.body: Unlike mollusks, humans shed their outer shells daily. Here they barter for dyed textiles printed with territorial emblems, obsolete musical ensembles, and optical shields.
stops.move: Stop at an outdoor rack. Touch three different shirts made of different fabric blends with your thumb and forefinger.
stops.image_query: St Marks Place street vendors New York

stops.title: Synthetic Fuel Dispenser
stops.body: The colony maintains emergency fueling depots operated by lone elders. This station has poured liquid glucose, milk solids, and pressurized seltzer into paper vessels since 1974.
stops.move: Hand over five dollars in cash. Order an egg cream. Drink it on the curb without altering your facial expression.
stops.image_query: Rays Candy Store neon Avenue A

stops.title: The Master Species Enclosure
stops.place: Tompkins Square Park Dog Run, Avenue B & 9th St
stops.body: A fenced reservation reveals the true hierarchy of the planet. Small furry quadrupeds run in circles while the tall bipeds stand along the perimeter, gathering canine excrement into plastic satchels as an act of devotion.
stops.move: Grip the chain-link fence with both hands. Stay motionless until one quadruped makes direct eye contact with you.
stops.image_query: Tompkins Square Park dog run New York
